claims.text: High thermal input from traditional fusion-welding repair creates a hot-cracking risk in the relevant high-value component.
The proposed intervention is electrospark deposition of a CoCrFeNi-based HEA coating reinforced with WC particles.
Electrospark deposition provides sufficiently low thermal input to reduce hot cracking relative to fusion welding.
Electrospark deposition can produce a thin, metallurgically bonded HEA-WC coating under controlled low-heat conditions.
The deposited coating will contain WC particles uniformly dispersed in an HEA matrix.
HEAs can possess high corrosion resistance and strong mechanical properties.
CoCrFeNi HEAs have an FCC structure and excellent ductility.
WC particles are very hard and can function as hard reinforcing phases.
The minimal thermal input of electrospark deposition prevents significant alteration of the substrate microstructure.
The HEA matrix and WC particles jointly delay surface-defect initiation under combined mechanical and corrosive stress.
The HEA-WC electrospark-deposited coating will have a lower incidence of hot cracking than fusion-welded repair.
The HEA-WC electrospark-deposited coating will increase surface hardness relative to fusion-welded and untreated surfaces.
The HEA-WC electrospark-deposited coating will improve wear resistance relative to fusion-welded and untreated surfaces.
The HEA-WC electrospark-deposited coating will improve corrosion resistance relative to fusion-welded and untreated surfaces.
Untreated surfaces in the intended service environment are prone to rapid wear and corrosion.
Electrospark deposition is suitable for localized repair when component geometry permits access to the damaged surface.
The intervention may not be suitable for large repairs requiring thick deposits.
Inadequate surface preparation can prevent effective metallurgical bonding of the coating.
The magnitude of hardness and wear improvements depends on alloy composition and electrospark-deposition process parameters.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in cracking, hardness, wear, and corrosion performance against both controls would falsify the hypothesis.
